text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigerian government appoints electoral commissioners for each of the 36 states and the capital territory Abuja.
- Provisional ruling council sets up high-powered commission to look into incessant fuel shortage in oil-producing Nigeria.
- Discharge of imported fuel delayed as navy refuses tanker clearance to dock for many hours.

- Foreign ministers of the Economic Community of West African States to meet in Conakry, Guinea, on Thursday to map out strategies for dealing with Sierra Leone coup which ousted the elected president.
- Civil servants demand higher pay to cope with economic difficulties facing them.
- Federal authorities revoke operating licences of 97 mortgage banks caught up in flagrant and continous breach of ethics.
- Professor Sam Aluko, head of government watchdog comittee on the economy, says Nigeria loses $100,000 to "cheats" on every 30,000 tonnes of imported fuel.
- Opposition NADECO says it is not aware of any plans to free presidential claimant Moshood Abiola as reported by a local newspaper.
- An official decision on whether or not to shift state governorship elections to next year from the last quarter of this year will be announced next week.
- As government's deadline of 48 hours within which to supply fuel passes, the precious commodity trickles into Lagos while many filling stations sell fuel under chaotic conditions.
